## What it is

To understand whether a clinically aligned vocabulary would differently benefit males and females, I leveraged machine models to predict clinical levels of depression, anxiety, and stress in males and females using a large data set (n = 39,775).  The goal of the project was to discover whether there are underlying gender differences in measure perfomance of the 21-item Depression Anxiety and Stress Scales (DASS-21).  Findings suggest that the DASS-21 measure performs differently for females with clinically high levels of depression than for males. No differences were found for anxiety and stress.

## What I did

- Conducted a literature review to form research questions
- Consulted the psychological literature on coding machine models
- Coded and applied machine models to a large data
- Wrote a research paper to report the results
